title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region residency with audit logging and RBAC policy mappings
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require strict data residency and KMS key locality guarantees. Previous RBAC v2 policy scaffolding supported region pinning at a high level but did not enforce residency at request time nor emit detailed audit events for KMS selection/fallbacks. This PR glues RBAC v2 policy mappings, KMS region residency enforcement, and audit logging so operator teams can both enforce and observe KMS residency decisions. Scope: enforcement middleware for KMS-residency, policy-to-KMS mapping update, new audit events for residency decisions and fallback reasons, CLI/helm config knobs, and docs/migration notes. Changes: (1) add enforcement middleware that consults RBAC v2 resource annotations and the new kms_residency policy store, returning 403 when a request tries to use a cross-region key when residency is enforced; (2) update KMS integration layer to surface region metadata and emit structured audit events (kms.region_decision, kms.fallback_reason); (3) map RBAC v2 actions to residency policies during policy evaluation to allow scoped exceptions (e.g., service-account backups); (4) add feature flag and helm values to enable strict residency by default for Private deployments; (5) add end-to-end unit and integration tests and docs page describing migration steps. Checklist: TODOs: update customer migration guide with example Linear/SEC tasks, coordinate with infra for rollout window. Testing performed: unit tests, e2e in perf-canary, manual verification with sample multi-region KMS fixtures. Migration notes: non-strict mode is opt-out; operators should audit kms.region_decision events for 1 week before enabling strict enforcement. Related: ENG-998, SEC-234, SUP-1287.
